_note: Version-3 kit design for the stimulus-generation pilot: pilot/prompts_v2/design.json with this note changed and one prompt example dropped, so every cell, the example negative control, the probe endings, the variant design and every other prompt example are version 2's. The dropped example is the second of rule 5's patient phrases: it named the whole organ, leaving out the side of the left-sided chamber that the example's leaflet wording describes, which rule 8 now forbids. Run 2 paired that chamber with the bare organ name twice (A__cardiology__body_part__L01 and B__cardiology__body_part__L08). Editing an existing example's value is a data change: it renders through the marker the example already has. harness_version stays 2: the version-3 kit changes the generation prompt's rule text and the value of one example, and nothing the scripts parse or count. The rules added for run 3 (first person only, common slang only, at most one brand-name concept per call, keep the side and the number, no grid names for a region, the clinical phrase as a clinician says it) are written in generation_prompt.txt as plain rule text, without example words. They could not be design.json settings: the version-2 harness renders only the markers listed in pilot/scripts/common.py (generation_markers) and refuses any other, so a rendered setting such as the brand-name cap would need a new marker, which is a script change that re-seals both recorded runs. prompt_examples render into the same markers as in version 2; in the version-3 prompt they illustrate rules 3, 4, 5, 7 and 10 (version 2's rules 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7; the comments in common.py's V2_PROMPT_EXAMPLES name the version-2 numbers). These are data, not code (engine AGENTS.md: medical vocabulary lives in data files, never in Python source). Copy this file into a run directory as design.json before planning; pilot/prompts_v3/README.md has what changed and why.
